proof:
Source: steps 4, 5, 6 and 8 of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary finite family. The parent applies it with m = d, Λ₁ᵢ = P_i and Λ₂ᵢ = V̂_i.
1. (Riesz–Markov–Kakutani.) For i ∈ Fin m let bᵢ := RealRMK.rieszMeasure Λ₁ᵢ and aᵢ := RealRMK.rieszMeasure Λ₂ᵢ. These are measures on the Borel σ-algebra of X. They are regular (RealRMK.regular_rieszMeasure), hence finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts). For every f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), ∫ f dbᵢ = Λ₁ᵢ f and ∫ f daᵢ = Λ₂ᵢ f (RealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure).
2. (Dominating measure.) Let μ₀ := Σ_{i ∈ Fin m} (aᵢ + bᵢ). For compact K, μ₀(K) = Σ_i (aᵢ(K) + bᵢ(K)) is a finite sum of finite terms, so μ₀(K) < ∞. Thus μ₀ is finite on compact sets. (For m = 0, μ₀ = 0.)
3. (σ-finiteness.) X is locally compact with a countable basis, hence σ-compact (sigmaCompactSpace_of_locallyCompact_secondCountable). A measure finite on compact sets of a σ-compact space is σ-finite (SigmaFinite.of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts). So μ₀ and all aᵢ, bᵢ are σ-finite, and each pair (ξ, μ₀) with ξ ∈ {aᵢ, bᵢ} has a Lebesgue decomposition.
4. (Absolute continuity.) Let s ⊆ X with μ₀(s) = 0. Then Σ_j (aⱼ(s) + bⱼ(s)) = 0 is a finite sum of elements of [0, ∞], so every term is 0; in particular aᵢ(s) = 0 and bᵢ(s) = 0. Hence aᵢ ≪ μ₀ and bᵢ ≪ μ₀.
5. (Density representation.) Let ξ be one of aᵢ, bᵢ, and let δ := ξ.rnDeriv μ₀ : X → [0, ∞], which is measurable (Measure.measurable_rnDeriv). The Lebesgue decomposition gives ξ = ξ.singularPart μ₀ + μ₀.withDensity δ (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add). Since ξ ≪ μ₀, ξ.singularPart μ₀ = 0 (Measure.singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac), so ξ = μ₀.withDensity δ. Moreover δ(x) < ∞ for μ₀-a.e. x (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top, since ξ is σ-finite).
6. (Local integrability of the densities.) Let K be compact. Since ξ(K) < ∞, ∫⁻_K δ dμ₀ < ∞ (Measure.lintegral_rnDeriv_lt_top_of_measure_ne_top). As δ is measurable, x ↦ (δ x).toReal is integrable for μ₀ restricted to K (integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top), i.e. μ₀-integrable on K.
7. (Integrals against ξ.) Let f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ).
 (a) Since ξ = μ₀.withDensity δ with δ measurable and finite μ₀-a.e., ∫ f dξ = ∫ (δ x).toReal·f(x) dμ₀(x) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul).
 (b) x ↦ (δ x).toReal·f(x) is μ₀-integrable. K_f := tsupport f is compact. f is continuous, hence Borel measurable, and bounded: |f(x)| ≤ C for all x, being continuous with compact support. By step 6, (δ ·).toReal is integrable on K_f, so the product is integrable on K_f (integrable times bounded measurable, Integrable.mul_bdd). It vanishes outside K_f, where f = 0, so it is integrable on X (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero).
8. (Definition of ρ.) Put αᵢ := aᵢ.rnDeriv μ₀, βᵢ := bᵢ.rnDeriv μ₀ and ρᵢ(x) := (βᵢ x).toReal − (αᵢ x).toReal. Each ρᵢ is measurable: toReal of a measurable [0, ∞]-valued function is measurable, and so is a difference of measurable functions. For compact K, ρᵢ is μ₀-integrable on K, as the difference of the two integrable functions given by step 6 for ξ = bᵢ and ξ = aᵢ.
9. (Representation.) For i ∈ Fin m and f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ):
 Λ₁ᵢ f − Λ₂ᵢ f = ∫ f dbᵢ − ∫ f daᵢ (step 1)
 = ∫ (βᵢ x).toReal·f(x) dμ₀ − ∫ (αᵢ x).toReal·f(x) dμ₀ (step 7(a))
 = ∫ ((βᵢ x).toReal − (αᵢ x).toReal)·f(x) dμ₀ (linearity of the integral; both integrands are integrable by step 7(b))
 = ∫ f(x)·ρᵢ(x) dμ₀(x).
10. Steps 2, 8 and 9 show that μ₀ and ρ have all the required properties.
key_steps: RMK: aᵢ := rieszMeasure Λ₂ᵢ and bᵢ := rieszMeasure Λ₁ᵢ are finite on compacts with ∫ f daᵢ = Λ₂ᵢ f and ∫ f dbᵢ = Λ₁ᵢ f.
μ₀ := Σᵢ (aᵢ + bᵢ) is finite on compacts; X is σ-compact, so μ₀, aᵢ, bᵢ are σ-finite; μ₀(s) = 0 forces aᵢ(s) = bᵢ(s) = 0, so aᵢ, bᵢ ≪ μ₀.
Lebesgue decomposition + singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac: ξ = μ₀.withDensity (ξ.rnDeriv μ₀), with a measurable, a.e.-finite density whose lintegral over each compact set is finite.
ρᵢ := (βᵢ).toReal − (αᵢ).toReal is measurable and integrable on compacts.
integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul plus integrability of density × f (bounded, compact support) gives Λ₁ᵢ f − Λ₂ᵢ f = ∫ f ρᵢ dμ₀.
